questions.explanation: Bearings are always measured clockwise from north and given as three-figure values.

questions.stem: The bearing of due east is:
questions.explanation: Due east is $90°$ clockwise from north, written as $090°$ in three-figure bearing format.

questions.stem: The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $065°$. What is the bearing of $A$ from $B$?
The bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is $310°$. What is the bearing of $P$ from $Q$?
A ship sails on a bearing of $135°$. In which general direction is it heading?
questions.explanation: $135°$ is halfway between south ($180°$) and east ($090°$), so the direction is south-east.

questions.stem: Town $A$ is due north of town $C$. Town $B$ is on a bearing of $070°$ from $A$. What is the angle $BAC$ in the triangle?
questions.explanation: Since $A$ is due north of $C$, the line $AC$ points south from $A$. The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $070°$ from north, so angle $BAC$ (measured between the north line and $AB$) is $70°$.

questions.stem: A plane flies from $P$ on a bearing of $040°$ for $200$ km, then turns to a bearing of $130°$ for $150$ km to reach $Q$. The angle of the turn at the intermediate point is:
questions.explanation: The reverse of bearing $040°$ is $220°$. The interior angle at the turning point $= 220° - 130° = 90°$.
